title: Arakawa–Suzuki Functors and Higher-Level Schur–Weyl Duality

items.title: The degenerate affine Hecke algebra
items.statement: Fix $d\ge0$. The degenerate affine Hecke algebra $H_d$ is the associative $\mathbb C$-algebra with underlying vector space $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes\mathbb C[S_d]$, in which $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes1$ and $\mathbb C[S_d]=1\otimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ are subalgebras and the cross relations $s_ix_j=x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$ and $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$ hold, where $s_i=(i\ i+1)$ is the $i$-th basic transposition. The algebra is generated by $x_1,\dots,x_d$ and $S_d$; the assignments $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\to H_d$ and $\mathbb C[S_d]\to H_d$ are injective, and the monomials $\{x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w: r_i\ge0,\ w\in S_d\}$ form a $\mathbb C$-basis. In particular $H_0=\mathbb C$, $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$, and for the quotient by $\langle x_1\rangle$ there is an isomorphism $H_d/\langle x_1\rangle\cong\mathbb C[S_d]$ sending $s_i$ to $s_i$ (the evaluation homomorphism at $0$). The algebra $H_d$ is the $\mathbb Z$-graded version of the affine Hecke algebra of $GL_d$: the generators $x_i$ are the Bernstein polynomial generators and $s_i$ the group-like generators in this degenerate presentation.
items.strategy: Check the two presentations dictionary: the relations $s_ix_j=x_js_i$ ($j\notin\{i,i+1\}$) and $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$ imply $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$ by multiplying on the left and right by $s_i$ and using $s_i^2=1$. The braid and quadratic relations for the $s_i$ come from the Coxeter presentation of $S_d$, and the $x_i$ pairwise commute since they sit in the polynomial subalgebra. Injectivity of the two subalgebras and the monomial basis are proved exactly as in [BK3, Lemma 3.5] and [BKAR, (3.8)] by triangular rewriting of words in the generators; the same argument gives the evaluation quotient at $x_1=0$. Do not confuse this algebra with the non-degenerate affine Hecke algebra: no quadratic relation is imposed on $x_i$, and the polynomial subalgebra is not truncated here.

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let $I\subset\mathbb Z$ be a set of consecutive integers and let $\Lambda=\sum_{i\in I}m_i\Lambda_i$ be a dominant weight of level $l=\sum m_i$ for the root system of type $A_\infty$ (so $m_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and $m_i=0$ for all but finitely many $i$). The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra of level $l$ is the quotient $H_d(\Lambda)=H_d/\langle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{m_i}\rangle$ of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra by the two-sided ideal generated by the level polynomial $\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{m_i}$. In the finite type-A pyramid formulation with column heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$ and origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$ one uses the quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by $\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-(c_j+q_j-n))$, written $H_d(\lambda,c)$; the identification $\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^l\Lambda_{c_j+q_j-n}$ matches the two conventions. The cosets of $\{x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w: 0\le r_i<l,\ w\in S_d\}$ form a basis, so $\dim H_d(\Lambda)=l^dd!$. The polynomial degree defines an increasing filtration $F_rH_d(\Lambda)$ with $\mathrm{gr}\,H_d(\Lambda)\cong C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$, the twisted tensor product of the truncated polynomial algebra $C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)$ with $\mathbb C[S_d]$ (with $s_ix_j=x_js_i$, $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i$ in the associated graded). If $l=1$ then $H_d(\Lambda)\cong\mathbb C[S_d]$ via $x_1\mapsto a$, $s_i\mapsto s_i$ for the unique $a$ with $m_a=1$, i.e. via the evaluation homomorphism. The anti-automorphism $\ast$ of $H_d$ with $x_i^\ast=x_i$ and $s_i^\ast=s_i$ descends to $H_d(\Lambda)$.
items.strategy: Descend the anti-automorphism and the filtration through the quotient; the quotient basis and dimension are obtained by reducing an arbitrary monomial in a fixed word of $H_d$ modulo $x_1$-relations using the cross relations, exactly as in [BKAR, (3.8)] (a proof is also in [BKHL, Lemma 3.5] and [BK3, Lemma 3.5]). The associated graded statement: the relations of the quotient imply that the surjection $C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]\to\mathrm{gr}\,H_d(\Lambda)$, $x_i\mapsto\mathrm{gr}_1x_i$, $s_j\mapsto\mathrm{gr}_0s_j$ is well defined, and injectivity follows because it maps a spanning set of distinct monomials to the basis monomials; this is [BKHL, Lemma 3.5]. The $l=1$ evaluation statement is the defining relation. Record that the reversal $s\mapsto s$, $x_i\mapsto x_i$ is an anti-automorphism, so the dualities of finitely generated modules below are well defined.

items.title: Arakawa-Suzuki Casimir operators on the tensor functors
items.statement: Let $V=\mathbb C^N$ be the natural $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$-module with basis $v_1,\dots,v_N$ and matrix units $e_{i,j}$, and let $\Omega=\sum_{i,j=1}^N e_{i,j}\otimes e_{j,i}\in\mathfrak g\otimes\mathfrak g\subset U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g)$ be the Casimir tensor of the trace form $(x|y)=\mathrm{tr}(xy)$. On the tensor functor $T_d(M)=M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ define: (i) $x_1\in\mathrm{End}(T_d)$ by the left action of $\Omega$ on the pair $(M,V_{(1)})$, i.e. $x_1=\sum_{i,j}e_{i,j}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}$; (ii) $s_i\in\mathrm{End}(T_d)$ for $1\le i<d$ by the left action of $\Omega$ on the pair $(V_{(i)},V_{(i+1)})$, i.e. $s_i=1^{\otimes i}\otimes\Omega\otimes1^{\otimes(d-i-1)}$, which is the place permutation of the $i$-th and $(i+1)$-th tensor factors because $\Omega$ acts on $V\otimes V$ as the flip; (iii) recursively $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ for $1\le j<d$. All $x_j$ and $s_i$ are natural in $M$, hence are endomorphisms of the functor $T_d$; they act on the $d=0$ case by $x_0$ omitted. The Arakawa-Suzuki normalization of [AS, (2.2.2)] realizes the same algebra with generators $y_i=\Omega_{0i}+\sum_{1\le j<i}(\Omega_{ji}+\tfrac1n)+\tfrac{n-1}2$ and $s_{ij}=\Omega_{ij}+\tfrac1n$ on $X\otimes V_n^{\otimes\ell}$; the two presentations are identified by $x_i\leftrightarrow y_i$, $s_i\leftrightarrow s_{i,i+1}$, and for $M$ concentrated in degree $0$ the action is the classical place permutation action of $\mathbb C[S_d]$.
items.strategy: Define $\Omega$ as the Casimir tensor of the trace form and verify by the basis computation $\Omega(v_a\otimes v_b)=v_b\otimes v_a$ that its action on $V\otimes V$ is the flip; this makes $s_i$ the place permutation and shows that $s_i^2=1$ and the braid relations hold on $V^{\otimes d}$. Then set the recursive definition of $x_j$; naturality of $x_1$ and of the flips is immediate from the $\mathfrak g$-module structure of $M$, and naturality of all $x_j$ follows by induction from the recursion. The dictionary with [AS, (2.2.2)] is a change of variables in the two presentations of the Hecke algebra and is recorded so that both source normalizations can be used; the comparison is exactly the statement that [BKHL, (3.10)-(3.12)] is the construction of [AS, Section 2.2].

items.title: The Casimir and place-permutation operators satisfy the degenerate affine Hecke relations
items.statement: For every $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$-module $M$ the endomorphisms $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ of $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ defined by the Casimir tensor $\Omega=\sum e_{i,j}\otimes e_{j,i}$ satisfy the defining relations of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra $H_d$, hence define a right action of $H_d$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ that commutes with the left action of $U(\mathfrak g)$ and is natural in $M$. Explicitly: $s_i^2=1$; $s_is_j=s_js_i$ for $|i-j|>1$; $s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$; $x_ix_j=x_jx_i$; $s_ix_j=x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$; and $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$, $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$. The only nontrivial identities are the braid relation and the cross relation, both of which reduce to the tensor identity $[\Omega_{12},\Omega_{23}]=[\Omega_{13},\Omega_{12}]$ in $U(\mathfrak g)^{\otimes3}$; the recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ then gives the remaining cross relations. For the augmented operators $y_i$ of [AS, Section 2.2] the same relations were verified directly in [AS, Lemma 2.2.1].
items.strategy: The involutions $s_i$ and the braid relations are the standard presentation of place permutations. For the cross relation compute on $M\otimes V\otimes V$ that $s_1x_2=\Omega_{12}\Omega_{23}$ and $x_1s_1+1=\Omega_{23}\Omega_{12}+1$; expanding the matrix units the difference is $[\Omega_{12},\Omega_{23}]-1$, and the classical identity $[\Omega_{12},\Omega_{23}]=[\Omega_{13},\Omega_{12}]$ together with the vanishing of $[\Omega_{13},\Omega_{12}]$ on the tensor product (the two terms are equal after the basis computation) gives the claim; alternatively follow [AS, Lemma 2.2.1], which proves $[y_i,y_j]=0$ and $s_iy_j-y_{s_i(j)}s_i=-\langle\alpha_i,\epsilon_j^\vee\rangle$ directly from $[\Omega_{ij}+\Omega_{jk},\Omega_{ik}]=0$ and $[\Omega_{ij},\Omega_{km}]=0$ for distinct indices. Commutation with $U(\mathfrak g)$ is immediate: $\Omega$ is $\mathfrak g$-invariant and the flips commute with the diagonal action. The recursion then propagates the relations to all $x_j$.

items.title: The parabolic highest-weight truncation factors through the cyclotomic quotient
items.statement: Fix $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$, a partition $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$, origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the level-$l$ weight $\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^l\Lambda_{c_j+q_j-n}$. On the twisted tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ (the module $V^{\otimes d}$ with the $\mathfrak p$-action twisted by the automorphism $\eta_c$ of $U(\mathfrak p)$ with $\eta_c(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}c_{\mathrm{col}(i)}$) the Casimir operator $x_1$ has minimal polynomial exactly $\prod_{j=1}^l(x-(c_j+q_j-n))$. Hence the right $H_d$-action on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ (and on every finitely generated module in the parabolic block $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ carrying its highest-weight filtration) factors through the quotient $H_d(\Lambda)=H_d(\lambda,c)$ of level $l$; the same holds for every standard module $N(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^d_c(\lambda)$, on which $x_1$ acts on the highest-weight part by the characters $c_{\mathrm{col}(i)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(i)}-n$ read off the $l$ columns. In particular the cyclotomic polynomial has degree $l$, and no smaller polynomial annihilates $x_1$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$.
items.strategy: Compute the associated graded: the loop filtration of $V_c^{\otimes d}$ has associated graded equal to the Vust tensor space with $\mathrm{gr}\,x_1=e\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}$; since $l$ is the size of the largest Jordan block of $e$, that graded operator has minimal polynomial exactly $x^l$, so the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ has degree at least $l$. Conversely, [BKHL, Lemma 3.4] computes the action on the standard modules: for $d=1$ the eigenvalues of $x_1$ on $V_c$ are exactly the $c_j+q_j-n$, $j=1,\dots,l$, and for $d\ge1$ the same polynomial divides the minimal polynomial by the explicit formula of [BKHL, Lemma 3.3] for the action of $x_1$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ (equivalently [BK3, Lemma 3.3]): the recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ shows that the eigenvalues of all $x_j$ are drawn from the same $l$-element set. Combine the two degree bounds. The highest-weight filtration statement follows because the filtration of $V_c^{\otimes d}$ by standard modules $V(A)$ is $\mathfrak p$-stable, so $x_1$ preserves it and the computation reduces to the standard modules.

items.title: The type-A nilpotent pyramid, good grading and Whittaker character
items.statement: Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$ and let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$. Number the boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left, write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for the row and column of the $i$-th box, let $L(i)$ be the number of the box immediately to the left of the $i$-th box (or $\emptyset$), and define the nilpotent $e=\sum_i e_{i,L(i)}\in\mathfrak g$, $v_i\mapsto v_{L(i)}$. Declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ and let $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0$, $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r$. Then $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$ (largest Jordan block $l$), $\mathfrak p$ is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor $\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak m$ is the nilradical of the opposite parabolic, $\mathfrak g^{e}$ is the graded subalgebra $\bigoplus_{r\ge0}(\mathfrak g_r\cap\mathfrak g^e)$ generated by the elements $e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k}$ for $s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ (where $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$ for $i\ge j$), and the elements $\xi_{i,j}=e_{i,j}+e_{L(i),L(j)}+\cdots$ for $(i,j)\in J$ form a basis of $\mathfrak g^e$. Finally set $\chi(x)=(x,e)=\mathrm{tr}(xe)$ for $x\in\mathfrak m$; then $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character, i.e. $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$. This grading is the type-A pyramid good grading, not the Dynkin grading of an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple; it is the one used for the finite W-algebra of the higher-level Schur-Weyl duality.
items.strategy: The Jordan type and the parabolic/Levi description are read off the diagram: multiplication by $e$ moves each box one step left, so the Jordan blocks are the rows of $\lambda$ and the largest block has size $l$. The description of $\mathfrak g^e$ and the basis $\{\xi_{i,j}\}$ is [BKHL, Section 2.1] (the map $J\to K$, $(i,j)\mapsto(\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{row}(j),\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i))$, is a bijection there). For the character: $\chi([x,y])=(e,[x,y])=([e,x],y)$ by invariance of the trace form. Write $x=\sum_{u>v}x_{u,v}e_{u,v}$, $y=\sum_{u>v}y_{u,v}e_{u,v}$ in the index order, where $u>v$ means $\mathrm{col}(u)>\mathrm{col}(v)$; then $[x,y]_{v,w}=\sum_k(x_{v,k}y_{k,w}-y_{v,k}x_{k,w})$ and the only nonzero contributions to $(e,[x,y])=\sum_{v=l(b)}[x,y]_{v,b}$ need $x_{v,k}\ne0$ and $y_{k,w}\ne0$, i.e. $k<v$ and $k>w$, impossible for the left-adjacent pair $v=L(b)$, $w=b$. Hence $\chi([x,y])=0$. Record that $\chi$ is the character used to define the Whittaker category in the next item.

items.title: The type-A finite W-algebra and the Whittaker category
items.statement: Keep the type-A pyramid data $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$ of the preceding item and let $\eta\colon U(\mathfrak p)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ be the algebra automorphism with $\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l)$ for all $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie character of the preceding item (so $I_\chi$ is the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$, $x\in\mathfrak m$) and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates. The type-A finite W-algebra is $W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p): [x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all } x\in\mathfrak m\}$; it is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a $(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule (the right action by $u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\eta(u)}$). The Whittaker category $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of $\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every $x\in\mathfrak m$; for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the Whittaker vectors $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M: xv=\chi(x)v\ \forall x\in\mathfrak m\}$ form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes $W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ (proved below): this is the loop or good filtration, not the Kazhdan filtration.
items.strategy: Show closedness of $W(\lambda)$ under multiplication and $\eta$-equivariance of the defining condition; the bimodule structure on $Q_\chi$ follows because $W(\lambda)$ preserves the left ideal $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ by definition. The $W(\lambda)$-module structure on $\mathrm{Wh}(M)$ follows from $[\mathfrak m,\eta(W(\lambda))]\subseteq U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$: for $m\in\mathfrak m$, $u\in W(\lambda)$ and a Whittaker vector $v$ one has $m(\eta(u)v)=\eta(u)mv+[m,\eta(u)]v=\chi(m)\eta(u)v$. The vanishing statement $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0\Rightarrow M=0$ is proved by the Gan-Ginzburg/Skryabin cohomology argument in the next-but-one item; record it here as part of the categorical interface. The dictionary $\eta$ is the type-A $\rho$-shift of [BKHL, Introduction] and is the one used (with the automorphism $\eta_c$) on tensor space.

items.title: The shifted Yangian and the pyramid generators of the type-A finite W-algebra
items.statement: Let $\sigma=(s_{i,j})$ be the shift matrix of the pyramid, $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$ for $i\ge j$. The shifted Yangian $Y_n(\sigma)$ is the associative $\mathbb C$-algebra with generators $D_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $r>0$), $E_{i,j}^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<j\le n$, $r>s_{i,j}$) and $F_{i,j}^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<j\le n$, $r>s_{j,i}$) subject to the shift-matrix Yangian relations of [BK3, Section 2]; it is graded by declaring $D_i^{(r)}$ to have degree $0$ and $E_{i,j}^{(r)}$ (resp. $F_{i,j}^{(r)}$) to have weight $\epsilon_i-\epsilon_j$ (resp. $\epsilon_j-\epsilon_i$), and filtered by the canonical filtration with all generators in degree $1$. The finite W-algebra $W(\lambda)$ is the quotient of $Y_n(\sigma)$ by the ideal generated by the elements $D_i^{(r)}$ for $r>p_i$ (the minimal admissible shape); under this quotient $W(\lambda)$ is generated by the images $T_{i,j}^{(r)}\in U(\mathfrak p)$ of the generators, $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for $r>S_{i,j}$ where $S_{i,j}=p_j+s_{i,j}$ for $i<j$, $S_{i,i}=p_i$, and the canonical filtration of $Y_n(\sigma)$ becomes the loop filtration of $W(\lambda)$ with $T_{i,j}^{(r)}\in F_rW(\lambda)$ and $\mathrm{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r)}=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}\in U(\mathfrak g^e)$ up to the standard sign. The $D$-generators $D_i^{(r)}$ (equivalently the elements of the Miura image) generate the polynomial part of $W(\lambda)$.
items.strategy: Specialize the general pyramid theory of [BK3, Chapters 2-3] to the left-justified diagram $\lambda$; the shift matrix and the generators are exactly those of [BK3, (2.54) and Section 3.4], with the identification of the quotient by the higher $D_i^{(r)}$ explained in [BK3, Section 3.4]. The grading and filtration conventions are those of [BK3, Section 2.2]; the sign in the leading symbol is [BK3, Lemma 3.4] and the vanishing range $r>S_{i,j}$ is [BK3, Theorem 3.5]. Record explicitly that this presentation is a $ℤ$-form over any commutative base ring. The PBW statement for the ordered monomials is separated into the next item.

items.title: Ordered monomial PBW basis for the shifted Yangian
items.statement: The shifted Yangian $Y_n(\sigma)$ has an ordered monomial basis: for any fixed total order on the generators $D_i^{(r)},E_{i,j}^{(r)},F_{i,j}^{(r)}$ of the preceding definition, the ordered monomials in these generators form a $\mathbb C$-basis of $Y_n(\sigma)$; consequently the canonical filtration is separated and $\mathrm{gr}\,Y_n(\sigma)$ is the free commutative algebra on the symbols of the generators. Moreover, in the quotient $W(\lambda)$ the ordered monomials in the surviving generators $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ with $r\le S_{i,j}$ form a basis, and accordingly $\mathrm{gr}\,W(\lambda)$ is the free commutative algebra on the leading symbols $\mathrm{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r)}$.
items.strategy: This is the PBW theorem for shifted Yangians [BK3, Section 2.2]: the proof is the usual triangular rewriting argument for the defining relations, by induction on the filtration degree, with the intertwining operators of [BK3, Sections 2.5-2.6] reducing the calculation to the rank-one case; the filtered algebra $\mathrm{gr}\,Y_n(\sigma)$ is identified with the symmetric algebra on the same generators by the associated graded of the PBW filtration. Pass to the quotient using [BK3, Theorem 3.5] (vanishing of $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ for $r>S_{i,j}$) and [BK3, Lemma 3.6], which states the graded freeness; the independence of the surviving ordered monomials is [BK3, Lemma 3.6].

items.title: Gan-Ginzburg and Skryabin inputs for the type-A pyramid good grading
items.statement: In the type-A pyramid situation, with $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r$ and $\chi(x)=(x,e)$, the following hold and admit the Gan-Ginzburg proof adapted to the pyramid good grading (as explicitly permitted by [BKHL, Section 3.3] and carried out for arbitrary good gradings in [BGK, Section 3]): (i) the form $\omega(x,y)=\chi([x,y])$ on $\mathfrak g_{-1}$ is nondegenerate, and choosing a Lagrangian $\ell\subset\mathfrak g_{-1}$ gives the $\chi$-admissible subalgebra $\mathfrak m_\ell=\ell\oplus\bigoplus_{r\le-2}\mathfrak g_r$, a nilpotent Lie algebra on which $\chi$ restricts to a character, with $Q_\ell=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak m_\ell)}\mathbb C_\chi$ and $W(\lambda)=Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ad}\,\mathfrak m_\ell}$ (independent of $\ell$ up to isomorphism); for the pyramid choice this recovers $W(\lambda)$ as defined above; (ii) the coadjoint action map $N_\ell\times S\to\chi+\mathfrak m_\ell^\perp$ is an isomorphism of affine varieties, and hence $\mathrm{gr}_KQ_\ell\cong\mathbb C[N_\ell]\otimes\mathrm{gr}_KW(\lambda)$ as graded modules; (iii) the Chevalley-Eilenberg complex of the $\chi$-twisted action of $\mathfrak m_\ell$ on $Q_\ell$ identifies with the algebraic de Rham complex of the unipotent group $N_\ell$, so that $H^0(\mathfrak m_\ell,Q_\ell)\cong W(\lambda)$ and $H^i(\mathfrak m_\ell,Q_\ell)=0$ for $i>0$; (iv) as a consequence, for every $\mathfrak g$-module $M$ in the Whittaker category $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ one has $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=H^0(\mathfrak m_\ell,M)=0\Rightarrow M=0$. All statements pass from $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ to $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ by splitting off the reductive centre, which acts by the central character and contributes only scalar or polynomial factors to the decomposition in (ii); the type-A pyramid in question is the left-justified diagram, for which the grading of the preceding items is a good grading compatible with the standard torus.
items.strategy: Adapt [GG, Sections 2, 4-6] from the Dynkin grading to the pyramid grading. For (i) use that $\chi$ restricts to a character on $\mathfrak m_\ell$ (verified in the preceding item in the type-A case, and in general because $[\mathfrak m_\ell,\mathfrak m_\ell]\subset\bigoplus_{r\le-2}\mathfrak g_r$ pairs to zero with $e\in\mathfrak g_1$); the equality $W(\lambda)=Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ad}\mathfrak m_\ell}$ is [BK3, Section 3.2]. For (ii) reproduce [GG, Lemma 2.1]: the coadjoint map is $C^*$-equivariant for the contracting action, induces an isomorphism on tangent spaces of the fixed points, and a contracting-action argument (with the graded character count) upgrades this to an isomorphism of affine varieties; the decomposition $\mathrm{gr}_KQ_\ell\cong\mathbb C[N_\ell]\otimes\mathrm{gr}_KW(\lambda)$ follows from the freeness of $\mathrm{C}[\mathfrak m_\ell^\perp]$ over $\mathrm{C}[S]$. For (iii) repeat [GG, Proposition 5.1-5.2]: compute $H^i(\mathfrak m_\ell,\mathrm{gr}_KQ_\ell)$ as invariants and higher coinvariants of the unipotent group, identify with the de Rham complex, and conclude vanishing by the spectral sequence. For (iv) use [GG, Theorem 6.1 proof]: if $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ then the kernel and cokernel of the canonical map $Q_\ell\otimes_{W(\lambda)}\mathrm{Wh}(M)\to M$ again have zero Whittaker vectors and vanish by (iii). The passage to $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ is the split-centre case; the ordinary Lie algebra cohomology interface is the published Chevalley-Eilenberg complex and its long exact sequence.

items.title: Skryabin's equivalence for the type-A Whittaker pair
items.statement: The functor $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor $\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$. For every finite dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor $?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the exact functor $M\mapsto M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X)$ on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a $W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map $\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X$, $(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x$, is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms $(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible, and for the one dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$ is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.
items.strategy: The equivalence and exactness are [GG, Theorem 6.1] (whose proof is the preceding item (iii)-(iv)); the same statement in the shifted Yangian setting is [BK3, Theorem 8.10] area. The isomorphism $\mu_{M,X}$ is [BK3, Theorem 8.1 and Corollary 8.2]: construct the inverse by the matrix $(y_{i,j})$ inverse to the matrix $(x_{i,j})$ from [BK3, Theorem 8.1] and check both composites on generators. The compatibility of the associativity isomorphisms is [BK3, (8.8)-(8.10)]; independence of the order in $\mu_d$ is [BKHL, (3.7)-(3.9)]. Verify the $\mathfrak p$-module case explicitly, since that is the only case used below; the construction is natural in $M$ and in $X$.

items.title: Vust's graded double centralizer for the type-A nilpotent centralizer
items.statement: Let $l$ be the number of columns of the pyramid and $C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)$ the truncated polynomial algebra, made into an algebra $C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ by the same cross relations as in $H_d$ (with $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i$ and $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i$), acting on the right of $V^{\otimes d}$ with $x_i$ acting as $1^{\otimes(i-1)}\otimes e\otimes1^{\otimes(d-i)}$ and $S_d$ by place permutations. Let $\varphi_d\colon U(\mathfrak g^e)\to\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V^{\otimes d})$ be the natural graded representation and $\psi_d$ the antihomomorphism from $C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ arising from the right action. Then $\varphi_d(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\mathrm{End}_{C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]}(V^{\otimes d})$ and $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g^e}(V^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}=\psi_d(C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d])$; moreover $\psi_d$ is injective whenever at least $d$ parts of $\lambda$ are equal to $l$. The first identity is a basis computation in the graded Schur algebra $\mathrm C[M_e]^*_d$ associated to the centralizer monoid $M_e=\{X: [X,e]=0\}$, and the second is Vust's theorem [KP, Section 6], a consequence of the normality of the closure of the conjugacy class of $e$.
items.strategy: Show that $\mathrm{End}_{C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]}(V^{\otimes d})$ consists of the invariant endomorphisms $\sum a_{i,j}e_{i,j}$ with coefficients constant on $S_d$-orbits, supported on the index pairs with $\mathrm{col}(i_k)\le\mathrm{col}(j_k)$ and stable under the left-shift operation $(i,j)\mapsto(R_k(i),R_k(j))$; this is the explicit calculation of [BKHL, Lemma 2.3]. The algebra $\mathrm C[M_e]^*_d$ with its basis $\xi_{i,j;r}$ and the surjection $\pi_d\colon U(\mathfrak g^e)\to\mathrm C[M_e]^*_d$ identify these endomorphisms with $\varphi_d(U(\mathfrak g^e))$, giving the first equality ([BKHL, Lemmas 2.1-2.2]). For the second equality use Vust's theorem: the normality of the closure of the conjugacy class of $e$ implies that the invariant-theoretic double centralizer property holds for $(U(\mathfrak g^e),C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d])$ on $V^{\otimes d}$; this is the theorem quoted in [BKHL, Theorem 2.4] from [KP, Section 6]. Injectivity in the stable range is proved directly in [BKHL, Theorem 2.4] by exhibiting a vector generating the regular module. Remark that by [BKHL, Remark 2.5] the first equality and the whole statement admit a formulation over an arbitrary commutative ring, using Donkin's positive-characteristic result in place of Vust; only the complex case is used below.

items.title: The loop filtration on the type-A finite W-algebra has associated graded U(g^e)
items.statement: Equip $W(\lambda)$ with the loop (good) filtration $F_rW(\lambda)=W(\lambda)\cap\bigoplus_{s\le r}U(\mathfrak p)_s$ induced by the pyramid grading $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$. Then the associated graded algebra $\mathrm{gr}\,W(\lambda)$ is canonically isomorphic to the enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, viewed as a graded algebra via the restriction of the pyramid grading to the centralizer $\mathfrak g^e$, and the isomorphism sends the leading symbol of the generator $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$ (with the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ the basis of $\mathfrak g^e$ of the previous items). In particular $W(\lambda)$ is a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and the loop filtration is separated: the ordered monomials in the generators $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$, form a basis of $W(\lambda)$. This filtration is not the Kazhdan filtration: the Kazhdan filtration has associated graded $\mathbb C[S]$ (a commutative Slodowy slice algebra), while here $\mathrm{gr}\,W(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative in general. Neither the loop filtration nor its associated graded requires the Kazhdan grading of the Gan-Ginzburg quantization.
items.strategy: Use the shifted-Yangian presentation: $W(\lambda)$ is generated by the $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ and its ordered monomials form a basis by the PBW theorem of the previous items; compute the leading symbols in the associated graded of $U(\mathfrak p)$ using [BKHL, Lemma 3.1] and [BK3, Lemma 3.4], which give $\mathrm{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)}=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. Since the $e_{i,j;r}$ form a basis of $\mathfrak g^e$ and satisfy the same PBW relations, comparing ordered monomials with the PBW basis of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ gives the algebra isomorphism. This is the proof of [BKHL, Lemma 3.1]; the same statement is [BGK, Theorem 3.8] for arbitrary good gradings, proved via the Kazhdan-filtration comparison with the Gan-Ginzburg quantization. Record explicitly that the filtration here is the good (loop) filtration: [BGK, Section 3.3] distinguishes it from the Kazhdan filtration, and only the former is used by the double centralizer argument.

items.title: The deformed tensor space for the type-A finite W-algebra
items.statement: Fix the pyramid $\lambda$, the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the truncated tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$: as a vector space it is $V^{\otimes d}$, it carries the left action of $U(\mathfrak p)$ twisted by $\eta_c$, $\eta_c(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}c_{\mathrm{col}(i)}$, and the right action of the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$, $\Lambda=\sum_{j}\Lambda_{c_j+q_j-n}$, defined on the generators by $s_i\mapsto$ place permutation of the $i$-th and $(i+1)$-th factors and $x_1\mapsto (e+\sum_{j=1}^N(q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j})\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\mathrm{col}(i)<\mathrm{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)}$ and $x_{j+1}\mapsto s_jx_js_j+s_j$; the action is well defined by the cyclotomic-quotient lemma. Restricting the left action from $U(\mathfrak p)$ to $W(\lambda)$ makes $V_c^{\otimes d}$ a filtered $(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The associated graded of this bimodule is the Vust tensor space: $\mathrm{gr}\,V_c^{\otimes d}\cong V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak g^e)$-action and the right $C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$-action of Vust's theorem, where $\mathrm{gr}\,x_1=e\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}$ and $\mathrm{gr}\,s_i$ is the place permutation. The canonical isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$ of Skryabin's equivalence is an isomorphism of $(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules, and the two actions commute: $W(\lambda)$ and $H_d(\Lambda)$ generate mutual centralizers of the filtered tensor space (proved in the next item).
items.strategy: Verify that the displayed assignment defines the right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action: on the associated graded it is the Vust action, and the cross relations were checked in [BKHL, Lemma 3.3] by reducing to the $x_1$-case through the recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$; the formula is exactly [BKHL, Introduction] and [BKHL, (3.7)-(3.9)]. The filtration is the tensor product of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ with the canonical filtration on $H_d(\Lambda)$; its associated graded is the Vust tensor space by the previous items. Commutation of the two actions is immediate from the construction (the left action is the restriction of the $U(\mathfrak p)$-action and the right action is built from $\eta_c$-twisted elements of $U(\mathfrak p)$ acting by the opposite multiplication). The bimodule structure on $\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}$ and the isomorphism $\mu_d$ are [BKHL, Section 3.3] and the previous item; check that both actions transport.

items.title: The finite-W and degenerate cyclotomic Hecke actions satisfy the double centralizer property
items.statement: Let $W_d(\lambda,c)$ be the image of $W(\lambda)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V_c^{\otimes d})$ and $H_d(\lambda,c)$ the image of $H_d(\Lambda)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Then $W(\lambda)$ maps into the centralizer of the $H_d(\Lambda)$-action and $H_d(\Lambda)$ into the centralizer of the $W(\lambda)$-action, and the two inclusions are equalities: $W_d(\lambda,c)=\mathrm{End}_{H_d(\Lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ and $H_d(\lambda,c)=\mathrm{End}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. At the level of associated graded algebras, $\mathrm{gr}\,W_d(\lambda,c)=\varphi_d(U(\mathfrak g^e))$ and $\mathrm{gr}\,H_d(\lambda,c)=\psi_d(C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d])$. Consequently the functor $\mathrm{Hom}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is an equivalence between $W_d(\lambda,c)$-mod and $H_d(\lambda,c)$-mod, and in the stable range (at least $d$ parts of $\lambda$ equal to $l$) the map $H_d(\Lambda)\to H_d(\lambda,c)$ is an isomorphism, so that this equivalence reads $W_d(\lambda,c)\text{-mod}\simeq H_d(\Lambda)\text{-mod}$.
items.strategy: Lift Vust's graded double centralizer through the separated loop filtration: Theorem 3.7 of [BKHL] proves that $\Phi_{d,c}(W(\lambda))=\mathrm{End}_{H_d(\Lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ and $\mathrm{End}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}=\Psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ by combining Vust's theorem on the associated graded with the filtered double centralizer lemma [BKHL, Lemma 3.6]: the associated graded centralizers are equal, and the general lemma on filtered centralizers transfers the equality back to the filtered subalgebras, using the identification of graded maps from the loop-filtration theorem. The stable-range injectivity is [BKHL, Lemma 3.5] and [BKHL, Theorem 2.4]. The last sentence is [BKHL, Theorem 5.10] (for the case $c=0$) plus the standard equivalence between modules over an endomorphism algebra and the projective-generator category; the case of general $c$ is identical with $\eta_c$ in place of $\eta$.

items.title: The Whittaker functor from the relevant parabolic category-O summand
items.statement:
Let $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the integral parabolic block of the preceding page for the type-A pyramid with origin $c$, let $O^d_c(\lambda)= igoplus_{\alpha:\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)=d}O^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the sum of the blocks generated by the modules $K(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^d_c(\lambda)$, and let $P_c=N(A_c)=K(A_c)$ be the unique (up to isomorphism) irreducible projective object of the ground block. The Whittaker functor is the exact functor $\mathcal V_c\colon O^d_c(\lambda)	o W(\lambda)	ext{-mod}$ defined on the bimodule $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}=P_c\otimes V_c^{\otimes d}$ by $\mathcal V_c(M)=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d},M)$ with the $W(\lambda)$-action induced from the $(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule structure of Skryabin's model, together with the natural isomorphism $
u\colon\mathcal V_c\circ(?\otimes V)	o(?\circledast V)\circ\mathcal V_c$ of functors; the pair $(\mathcal V_c,
u)$ satisfies: (V1) $\mathcal V_c(K(A))\cong L(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^d_c(\lambda)$ and $\mathcal V_c(K(A))=0$ otherwise, where $L(A)$ is the irreducible $W(\lambda)$-module of type $A$; and (V2) the two compatibility diagrams with the endomorphisms $x$ and $s$ of the functors $?\otimes V$ and $(?\otimes V)\otimes V$ commute. The functor is independent, up to unique isomorphism, of all choices: any exact functor $O_c(\lambda)	o W(\lambda)	ext{-mod}$ with a natural isomorphism $
u$ satisfying (V1)-(V2) is uniquely isomorphic to $\mathcal V_c$ with the isomorphism compatible with $
u$. Finally, $\mathcal V_c(P_c)\cong\mathbb C_c$ and the induced isomorphisms $j_d\colon\mathcal V_c(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})	o V_c^{\otimes d}$ are isomorphisms of $(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodules.
items.strategy: Construct $\mathcal V_c$ from the Whittaker vectors: [BK3, Section 8.5] defines the functor $\mathcal V$ on $O(\lambda)$ by $\mathcal V(M)=\mathrm{Wh}(M)$-type formulas and proves (V1) as [BK3, Theorem 8.21]; the compatibility (V2) is checked in [BK3, Lemma 8.19]. The bimodule isomorphism $j_d$ is [BKHL, (5.1)] and Lemma 5.5. Uniqueness is [BKHL, Theorem 5.17]; the proof fixes the scalar by $i_0\colon\mathcal V(P_c)\cong\mathbb C_c$ and reruns the construction of $\gamma,\sigma,\tau$. The identification $\mathcal V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})\cong V_c^{\otimes d}$ uses Skryabin's equivalence and the isomorphism $\mu_d$ of the deformed tensor space. Note that $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ is a self-dual projective generator in $O^d_c(\lambda)$ ([BKHL, Corollary 4.6, Theorem 4.8, Corollary 4.9]), the structured statement supplied by the preceding page.

items.title: The Whittaker functor is exact and fully faithful on the required projectives
items.statement: Let $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ be the self-dual projective generator of the block sum $O^d_c(\lambda)$ and let $T^\Lambda_\alpha$, $\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)=d$, be its block components. The Whittaker functor $\mathcal V_c$ is exact, and the natural transformation $\gamma\colon\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d},-)\to\mathrm{Hom}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)\circ\mathcal V_c$, $f\mapsto\mathcal V_c(f)\circ j_d^{-1}$, is an isomorphism of functors from $O^d_c(\lambda)$ to $H_d(\Lambda)$-modules; hence $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d},-)$ is fully faithful on projective objects and so is $\mathcal V_c$ on the projective objects it detects. Moreover $\mathcal V_c$ maps projective objects to projective modules: $\mathcal V_c(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})\cong V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a projective generator for the category of finitely generated $W_d(\lambda,c)$-modules. The composition of the equivalence $\mathrm{Hom}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)\colon W_d(\lambda,c)\text{-mod}\to H_d(\lambda,c)\text{-mod}$ with $\mathcal V_c$ is the quotient functor of $O^d_c(\lambda)$ by the Serre subcategory generated by the irreducibles $K(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^d_c(\lambda)$.
items.strategy: The isomorphism $\gamma$ is [BKHL, Lemma 5.11]; its proof reduces to the irreducibles using exactness of both sides and Corollary 4.9 plus Lemma 5.7, and checks that for $A=B$ the map $\mathcal V_c$ sends a surjection onto the simple $L(A)$ to a non-zero map of one-dimensional Hom spaces. Exactness of $\mathcal V_c$ is part of the definitions/Skryabin equivalence; the projective generator statement is [BKHL, Theorem 5.10], whose proof uses Corollaries 4.6, 4.9 and Theorem 4.8 to identify the summands of $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ with the $P(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^d_c(\lambda)$, and then Lemma 5.7 to identify $\mathcal V_c(P(A))$ as the projective cover of $L(A)$. The quotient-functor statement is [BKHL, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15]. The self-dual projective generator input is the preceding page's tilting/prinjectivity theorem.

items.title: The higher-level Schur-Weyl projective generator and Schur functor
items.statement: Fix the type-A pyramid $\lambda$, the origin $c$ and $d\ge0$. The higher-level Schur-Weyl projective generator is $T^\Lambda_\alpha=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ projected onto the block $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ (equivalently $T^\Lambda_\alpha=\bigoplus_{i\in I_\alpha}f_{i_d}\cdots f_{i_1}P_c$), and $T^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha}T^\Lambda_\alpha$; the module $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ is a ($\mathfrak g$,$H^\Lambda_\alpha$)-bimodule and $H^\Lambda_\alpha\cong\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the right action of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. The higher-level Schur functor is $\pi_\alpha=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha,-)\colon O^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, with left adjoint $\pi^*_\alpha=T^\Lambda_\alpha\otimes_{H^\Lambda_\alpha}-$; on the level of the locally unital algebra $H^\Lambda=\bigoplus_\alpha H^\Lambda_\alpha$ the two functors assemble into $\pi=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda,-)$ and $\pi^*=T^\Lambda\otimes_{H^\Lambda}-$. The endomorphism action is the opposite action: for $f\in\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)$ and $h\in H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with the bimodule structure $T^\Lambda_\alpha$, the identification $H^\Lambda_\alpha=\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}$ uses the composition convention opposite to the action on the second factor, and $\pi$ is a quotient functor; $\pi$ and $\pi^*$ are exact, $\pi$ is a quotient functor in the sense of Gabriel, and $\pi^*\pi$ preserves projectives. These constructions require the full additive closure over all integral central characters and hence the Axiom of Choice for the formation of the localizations and direct sums; AC is declared here and inherited by all consumers on this page.
items.strategy: Assemble $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ from the residue functors $f_i$ and the block projection of the preceding page, using the fact that the block projection is the action of the central idempotent $e_\alpha$; this is [BKAR, (3.27)-(3.28)]. The algebra isomorphism is [BKAR, Theorem 3.6] and [BKHL, Theorem 5.13]; the exactness of $\pi$ and the left adjunction of $\pi^*$ are the standard quotient-functor facts for a projective generator, recorded in [BKAR, Section 3.5]. Check the opposite-endomorphism convention carefully: $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ acts on $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ on the right, and the identification with $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}$ sends $h$ to left multiplication by $h$; do not identify it with the endomorphism algebra without the op. AC is used only to choose the decomposition data and the localizations over the possibly infinite block sum.

items.title: Stable range and block idempotent corner for higher-level Schur-Weyl duality
items.statement: The stable range for the type-A pyramid $\lambda$ in degree $d$ is the condition that at least $d$ parts of $\lambda$ are equal to $l$ (equivalently $\sum_{j=1}^{d}(l-q_j)=0$, i.e. the first $d$ columns of the diagram have full height $n$). In the stable range the natural map $\Psi_d\colon H_d(\Lambda)\to\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$ is injective, so $H_d(\lambda,c)\cong H_d(\Lambda)$ and the Hecke action is faithful; outside the stable range $H_d(\lambda,c)$ is a proper image, equal to a sum of blocks of $H_d(\Lambda)$, and there is a central idempotent $f\in H_d(\Lambda)$ with $H_d(\lambda,c)\cong fH_d(\Lambda)f$, concretely $\Psi_d$ induces an algebra isomorphism $fH_d(\Lambda)f\to H_d(\lambda,c)$ for the idempotent whose support is the set of contractible weights. Thus outside the stable range the correct algebra for the double centralizer statements is the corner $fH_d(\Lambda)f$, not the full $H_d(\Lambda)$; the block idempotent $f$ is the sum of the block idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ of the weight spaces whose tableaux $\mathbf i$ can be contracted to a tableau of the smaller pyramid $\bar\lambda$.
items.strategy: The stable-range injectivity is [BKHL, Lemma 3.5] (via the last part of Theorem 2.4): exhibit a vector $v_{\mathbf i}$ whose orbit under the truncated polynomial part generates a copy of the regular module $C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. Outside the stable range, [BKHL, Theorem 6.6] and [BKHL, Corollary 6.7] construct the central idempotent $f$ by separating the contractible weights from the non-contractible ones (Lemma 6.5: contractible and non-contractible weights have different central characters), and show that $fH_d(\lambda,c)f\cong H_d(\bar\lambda,c)$ for the trimmed pyramid; this is the corner structure. The block idempotents are the orthogonal idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ of the weight-space decomposition of $H_d(\Lambda)$; their sum over the contractible weights is $f$. Note that the direction of the claim is one-way: the Hecke action alone does not determine the algebra without either the stable-range condition or the corner.

items.title: Higher-level Schur-Weyl endomorphism isomorphism
items.statement: For every $\alpha\in Q^+$ of height $d$, the natural right action of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ on $T^\Lambda_\alpha=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ induces an algebra isomorphism $H^\Lambda_\alpha\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}$; here $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the block of $H^\Lambda$ and in the stable range it equals the full degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra $H_d(\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}$ read off the origin and the column heights. Equivalently, in the formulation of the higher-level Schur algebra: $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}=H_d(\lambda,c)$, where $H_d(\lambda,c)$ is the image of $H_d(\Lambda)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. The theorem includes surjectivity (the image of $H_d(\Lambda)$ is the full endomorphism algebra) as well as the matching dimension/injectivity in the stable range; outside the stable range the target is the image algebra $H_d(\lambda,c)=fH_d(\Lambda)f$ of the preceding Definition.
items.strategy: Combine [BKHL, Theorem 5.13] (from the bimodule isomorphism $j_d$ and Lemma 5.11) with the block projection $e_\alpha$: the standard g-equivariant projection of $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ onto $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the action of the central idempotent $e_\alpha$, so the endomorphism algebra of $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ is exactly $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ ([BKAR, Theorem 3.6], citing [BK3, Theorem 5.13], [BK3, Corollary 6.7] and [B2, Lemma 5.8]). Surjectivity is the content of the commuting diagram of [BKHL, Corollary 5.12]; injectivity/dimension in the stable range is [BKHL, Lemma 3.5]. Check that the right action used is the transported action through Skryabin's equivalence, and that the $\mathrm{op}$ convention matches the action on tensor space.

items.title: Higher-level Schur-Weyl double centralizer and full faithfulness on projectives
items.statement: The higher-level Schur-Weyl double centralizer holds: (i) $W_d(\lambda,c)=\mathrm{End}_{H_d(\lambda,c)}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ and $H_d(\lambda,c)=\mathrm{End}_{W_d(\lambda,c)}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the functor $\mathrm{Hom}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is an equivalence between $W_d(\lambda,c)$-mod and $H_d(\lambda,c)$-mod; (ii) the Schur functor $\pi_\alpha=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha,-)$ is fully faithful on projective objects and on tilting objects of $O^\Lambda_\alpha$; (iii) $\pi_\alpha$ is a quotient functor with exact left adjoint $\pi^*_\alpha$, and the composition with the Whittaker functor is the canonical quotient of $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ by the Serre subcategory of non-standard irreducibles. In particular the second centralizer of the finite-W image in the parabolic category is computed by the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke block, and no faithfulness is asserted outside the stable range beyond the corner statement of the preceding Definition.
items.strategy: Part (i) is Theorem A of [BKHL] (Theorem 5.10 together with Theorem 3.7); the equivalence is the standard endomorphism-algebra equivalence for the projective generator $V_c^{\otimes d}$ of the category of $W_d(\lambda,c)$-modules. Part (ii) is [BKAR, Theorem 3.7(vi)]: full faithfulness on projectives is [BK3, Theorem 6.10] (Stroppel's parabolic Struktursatz), and on tiltings it follows from Theorem 3.7(v) since heads and socles of tiltings have only standard labels. Part (iii) is [BKHL, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15]. Verify that all functors are restricted to the relevant summand of parabolic category O and that the quotient is taken in the Serre sense.

items.title: Hecke induction and restriction functors on degenerate cyclotomic blocks
items.statement: Let $H^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the block decomposition of the (locally unital) degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra of the preceding items, and let $e_\alpha\in H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the identity of the block (a central idempotent of $H^\Lambda$). The Hecke induction and restriction functors attached to a simple root $\alpha_i$ are the exact functors $f_i\colon\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)\to\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i})$ and $e_i\colon\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i})\to\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ defined by $f_iM=H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\otimes_{H^\Lambda_\alpha}M$ and $e_iN=e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}N$, where $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\in H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ is the idempotent projecting onto the weight spaces with $\mathbf i_{d+1}=i$. The functors $e_i,f_i$ are biadjoint, exact, they commute with the duality $\circledast$ ($M^\circledast=$ the dual space with action via the anti-automorphism $\ast$), and on the Grothendieck groups they are adjoint with respect to the Cartan pairing $\langle[P],[M]\rangle=\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{H^\Lambda}(P,M)$. The construction uses the embeddings $\iota\colon H_d\hookrightarrow H_{d+1}$ and the block idempotents $e_\alpha$; record that the unit and counit are the natural inclusion/projection maps, and that no choices beyond the finite block decomposition are needed, so the construction is choice-free except where the block sum is infinite (AC declared there).
items.strategy: Define the non-unital algebra homomorphism $\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ as the composite of the embedding $H_d\hookrightarrow H_{d+1}$ with multiplication by $e_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$; its image is $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$ with $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}=\sum_{\mathbf i\in I_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\mathbf i_{d+1}=i}e(\mathbf i)$. Then $f_iM=$(induced module) and $e_iN=$(the $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$-weight space) are as displayed. Biadjunction is the standard Frobenius reciprocity for induction and restriction along a non-unital homomorphism, and biadjoint functors are exact. The commutation with duality and the Cartan-pairing adjointness are [BKAR, Section 3.3, (3.16)-(3.20) and the remarks following (3.19)]; the proof is a direct computation with $\ast$.

items.title: Schur functor images of standard, simple, projective and tilting objects
items.statement: Under the Schur functor $\pi=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda,-)$: (i) the parabolic Verma module $N(A)$ maps to the Specht module $S(A)$, $\pi(N(A))\cong S(A)$; (ii) the irreducible $K(A)$ maps to $D(A)=\pi(K(A))$, which is irreducible if $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ and zero otherwise, and the family $\{D(A):A\in\mathrm{Std}\}$ is a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic irreducibles of $H^\Lambda$; (iii) the projective cover $P(A)$ maps to the cover $Y(A)=\pi(P(A))$ of $D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, and $\pi^*(\pi(P(A)))\cong P(A)$; (iv) the indecomposable tilting module $T(A)$ maps to a module whose standard/Specht filtration multiplicities are the opposite-parabolic/Arkhipov-Soergel coefficients, so that $[T(A)]$ is identified with the canonical basis element and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings. The multiplicities of Specht modules are given by Kazhdan-Lusztig values: $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):K(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$. All statements are at $q=1$ (the categorification level) and the images are taken in the block $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of the corresponding height.

The multiplicities $[N(A):K(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$ are [BKAR, Theorem 3.1(i)(a)] (the Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture in this setting) and the Specht-composition statement is [BKAR, Theorem 3.10(iii)]. items.title: Category-O translation intertwines residue induction and restriction
items.statement: There are natural isomorphisms of functors $f_i^{H}\circ\pi\cong\pi\circ f_i^{O}$ and $e_i^{H}\circ\pi\cong\pi\circ e_i^{O}$, where $f_i^{O},e_i^{O}$ are the special projective residue functors on the sum of parabolic category-O blocks of the preceding page (tensoring with the natural module and its dual, then projecting onto the block of the appropriate height) and $f_i^{H},e_i^{H}$ are the Hecke induction/restriction functors of the preceding Definition. The isomorphism is compatible with the biadjunctions on both sides, with the block projections $e_\alpha$, and with the gradings: on the Grothendieck groups the operators induced by $f_i^{O},e_i^{O}$ and $f_i^{H},e_i^{H}$ agree, and consequently the Schur functor identifies the Chevalley operators on $[O^\Lambda]$ and on $[\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)]$. In addition, $\pi$ commutes with the dualities, $\pi\circ\circledast\cong\circledast\circ\pi$, and with the parity of the gradings in the sense that it sends the graded residue filtration to the Hecke residue filtration. These natural isomorphisms are the categorical form of the fact that the higher-level Schur functor is a morphism of module categories over the type-A quantum group at $q=1$.
items.strategy: Construct the $-\otimes V$ side: for $M\in O^\Lambda_\alpha$ one has $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i},M\otimes V)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha,M)$ by adjunction of the residue functors, and $T^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ is a summand of $T^\Lambda_\alpha\otimes V$; this gives $f_i^{H}\circ\pi\cong\pi\circ f_i^{O}$ as in [BKAR, Theorem 3.7(iv)] and [BKHL, Lemma 5.16] (the isomorphism $\tau$ there is exactly this adjunction, with the Hecke induction $\mathrm{ind}^{d+1}_d$). The $e_i$-statement follows from the biadjunctions and the exactness of $\pi$. Commutation with duality is [BKAR, Theorem 4.5]. Grading conventions: the residue functors are the $i$-eigenspace/generalized eigenspace projections of the tensor/dual tensor action, and the Hecke side uses the residue idempotents $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$; the two must be matched by the dictionary of the preceding page's residue-translation items, not by an unproved identification of labels.

items.title: The degenerate affine Hecke relations on two tensor factors
items.statement: Take $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$, $V=\mathbb C^2$, $M=V$ and $d=2$, so that $M\otimes V^{\otimes2}=V^{\otimes3}$ has basis $v_a\otimes v_b\otimes v_c$. Compute $x_1=\Omega_{01}=e_{11}\otimes e_{11}\otimes1+e_{12}\otimes e_{21}\otimes1+e_{21}\otimes e_{12}\otimes1+e_{22}\otimes e_{22}\otimes1$ and $s_1=\Omega_{12}=1\otimes e_{11}\otimes e_{11}+1\otimes e_{12}\otimes e_{21}+1\otimes e_{21}\otimes e_{12}+1\otimes e_{22}\otimes e_{22}$, and set $x_2=s_1x_1s_1+s_1=\Omega_{02}+s_1$. Verify the defining relations of $H_2$ on each basis vector: $s_1^2=1$, $x_1x_2=x_2x_1$, $s_1x_2=x_1s_1+1$ and $x_2s_1=s_1x_1+1$. For example, on $v_1\otimes v_2\otimes v_1$ one computes $x_1s_1(v_1\otimes v_2\otimes v_1)=v_1\otimes v_1\otimes v_2+?$; carry out the computation for all eight basis vectors and check that the two sides agree, and note that in this normalization $s_1x_2\ne x_2s_1$ precisely by the commutator term $+1$.
items.strategy: Expand the matrix units on the standard basis and use $\Omega(v_a\otimes v_b)=v_b\otimes v_a$; then $x_2=\Omega_{02}+s_1$ is verified by the conjugation identity $s_1\Omega_{01}s_1=\Omega_{02}$. The relations are the $d=2$ case of the previous theorem; this example checks them by hand on all eight basis vectors, including at least one vector with repeated indices (where the flip contributes a fixed vector) and one with distinct indices. The two sides of $s_1x_2=x_1s_1+1$ differ by the identity term, so the example also shows that the cross relation is not a mere commutation.

items.title: A level-two cyclotomic polynomial from the highest-weight filtration
items.statement: Take $\lambda=(p_1,p_2)=(2,1)$, so $N=3$, $n=2$, $l=2$, $q=(2,1)$, and the origin $c=(0,0)$; then $\Lambda=\Lambda_{c_1+q_1-n}+\Lambda_{c_2+q_2-n}=\Lambda_0+\Lambda_{-1}$ and the level polynomial is $x(x+1)$. Boxes: $1=(1,1)$, $2=(2,1)$, $3=(1,2)$; $e=e_{1,3}$ (so $v_3\mapsto v_1$, $v_2\mapsto0$) has Jordan type $(2,1)$ with largest block $l=2$. On $V_c=V$ the operator $x_1=e+\sum_j(c_{\mathrm{col}(j)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}$ is the matrix (in the basis $v_1,v_2,v_3$) with $e_{1,3}$ and diagonal entries $0,0,-1$; it has eigenvalues $0$ and $-1$, each with multiplicity one and two respectively, and minimal polynomial exactly $x(x+1)=\prod_{j=1}^2(x-(c_j+q_j-n))$. On $V_c^{\otimes d}$ the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ is again exactly $x(x+1)$ (degree $l=2$), by the associated-graded argument: $\mathrm{gr}\,x_1=e\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}$ has minimal polynomial $x^2$. The quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$ has dimension $2^dd!$, and for $d=1$ the Hecke action on $V_c$ factors through $\mathbb C[x]/(x(x+1))\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C$, decomposing $V_c$ into the two generalized eigenspaces $\ker x_1$ (spanned by $v_1,v_2$) and $\ker(x_1+1)$ (spanned by $v_3$).
items.strategy: Compute $e$ and the diagonal shift box by box and write the $3\times3$ matrix of $x_1$; read off its minimal polynomial. For $d\ge1$ use the associated-graded computation of [BKHL, Lemma 3.4]: the loop filtration of $V_c^{\otimes d}$ has $\mathrm{gr}\,x_1=e\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}$, whose minimal polynomial is the square of the minimal polynomial of $e$ on $V$, i.e. $x^2$; hence the degree of the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ is exactly $l=2$, and its two roots are the eigenvalues of $x_1$ on $V$. Identify the roots with $c_j+q_j-n$ and verify the highest-weight filtration: the standard modules in the block have highest weights with entries shifted by $c_j$, so the cyclotomic roots on the highest-weight part are the same two scalars. The dimension $2^dd!$ is the basis count of the cyclotomic quotient.

items.title: Vust's double centralizer in a small stable range
items.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$, so $n=2$, $l=1$, $q_1=2$, $N=2$, $e=e_{1,2}$, all boxes in one column and the grading is concentrated in degree $0$: $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $\mathfrak m=0$, $C_1[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\mathbb C$, and $C_1[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]=\mathbb C[S_d]$. Verify Vust's double centralizer for $d=1,2$, which is the stable range for this $\lambda$ (at least $d$ parts equal to $l=1$ holds for $d\le2$). For $d=1$: $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V)=\mathbb C\cdot1=\psi_1(\mathbb C[S_1])$ and $\varphi_1(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V)$, as $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\to\mathrm{End}(V)$ is surjective. For $d=2$: $V^{\otimes2}=S^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$, $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes2})=2=\dim\mathbb C[S_2]$ with $\psi_2$ injective, and $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb C[S_2]}(V^{\otimes2})=\dim\mathrm{End}(S^2V)+\dim\mathrm{End}(\Lambda^2V)=9+1=10=\dim\varphi_2(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))$; check the two decompositions explicitly (the flip acts as $+1$ on $S^2V$ and $-1$ on $\Lambda^2V$, and the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ is exactly the block-diagonal algebra of the two isotypic components).
items.strategy: Compute in the standard basis: $e=e_{1,2}$ gives the single-block grading, so $\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak g$ and $\mathfrak m=0$. For $d=1$ the statements reduce to the surjectivity of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\to\mathrm{End}(V)$ and $\mathbb C[S_1]=\mathbb C$. For $d=2$ use the classical decomposition $V^{\otimes2}=S^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$ and the symmetrizer/antisymmetrizer $\frac{1\pm s_1}2$; the centralizer of the flip is $\mathrm{End}(S^2V)\times\mathrm{End}(\Lambda^2V)$, of dimension $10$, and the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ is easily checked to be its diagonal copy along the two isotypic components, hence equal to it. This is the level-one case where Vust's theorem reduces to the classical Schur-Weyl double centralizer; the published Schur-Weyl double centralizer theorem for $\mathbb C[S_d]$ and $\mathfrak{gl}(V)$ gives the same conclusion and is a check on the computation.

items.title: A block idempotent corner outside the stable range
items.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$ (so $l=1$, two parts equal to $1$) and $d=3$: the stable range fails, because at least $3$ parts of $\lambda$ equal to $1$ is false. Here $H_3(\Lambda)=\mathbb C[S_3]$ (level $l=1$), of dimension $6$, while the image $H_3(\lambda,c)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}$, $V=\mathbb C^2$, has dimension $5$: for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $V^{\otimes3}=L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$, so $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ has dimension $1+4=5$, and it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Under the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ (trivial, sign and standard blocks), the map to $\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ kills exactly the sign block; hence $H_3(\lambda,c)\cong f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ with $f$ the central idempotent of the trivial and standard blocks, and $f$ is the block idempotent corner of the Definition. Verify: $\dim f\mathbb C[S_3]f=1+4=5$, the map $\mathbb C[S_3]\twoheadrightarrow f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ is multiplication by $f$, and the antisymmetrizer $a=\sum_{w\in S_3}\mathrm{sgn}(w)w$ spans the kernel of the action on $V^{\otimes3}$ because $\Lambda^3V=0$ for $\dim V=2$.
items.strategy: Decompose $V^{\otimes3}$ for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ by the classical Schur-Weyl rule: the partitions of $3$ with at most $2$ rows are $(3)$ and $(2,1)$, so $V^{\otimes3}\cong L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$; hence $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})\cong\mathbb C\times M_2$, of dimension $5$, and by Schur-Weyl duality it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Compare with the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2$: the sign block acts on $V^{\otimes3}$ by zero because the sign representation does not occur in $V^{\otimes3}$ (equivalently $\Lambda^3V=0$), so the kernel is the sign block and the image is the corner of the other two blocks. The dimension count and the corner identification verify the general statement of the preceding Definition in the smallest non-stable case.

items.title: A Hecke action alone does not imply the double centralizer property
items.statement: Let $M=\mathbb C^2$ be the trivial $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$-module, $V=\mathbb C^2$ the natural module and $d=1$. The Arakawa-Suzuki construction provides an action of $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$ on $M\otimes V\cong\mathbb C^4$ commuting with $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, but here $x_1=\Omega^{M,V}=0$, so the action is the evaluation action $x_1\mapsto0$ and $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(\mathbb C^4)=M_4(\mathbb C)$. On the other hand the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ in $\mathrm{End}(M\otimes V)$ is the subalgebra $1_{\mathbb C^2}\otimes M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension $4$. Hence the equality $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=\mathrm{End}_{H_d}(M\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ fails by a factor of $4$ in dimension, even though the Hecke action is genuine, commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and is natural in $M$. The other equality also fails: $\psi(H_1)=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}\subsetneq\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(M\otimes V)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\otimes1$, of dimension $4$. The hypothesis that is missing is the truncated/deformed setup: the double centralizer theorem applies to the finite-W-algebra tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ over the pyramid (equivalently to $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ with the truncated polynomial algebra $C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$), where the Hecke action is the cyclotomic quotient action and the algebra of the opposite side is the finite W-algebra, not $U(\mathfrak g)$.
items.strategy: Compute $x_1$ on $M\otimes V$: the Casimir tensor has its first tensor factor acting on the trivial module $M$, so $x_1=0$; this is a legitimate instance of the Arakawa-Suzuki action, since the construction assigns an $H_d$-action to every $\mathfrak g$-module $M$. Compute the two centralizers in the bases $\{u_a\otimes v_b\}$: $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)$ is all of $M_4$ because $H_1$ acts by scalars, while $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=1\otimes M_2$ has dimension $4$; the other centralizer is $M_2\otimes1$ versus $\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}$. Hence both double centralizer equalities fail. This is not a counterexample to the higher-level Schur-Weyl theorem: it shows that the theorem needs the finite-W-algebra deformation/truncation hypotheses, and that a mere commuting Hecke action on an arbitrary tensor module is insufficient.
